description:
## Problem

`run_osd_campaign` drives its per-block evaluator through a sequential `FnMut(OsdBlockContext<'_>) -> OsdBlockOutcome` loop, so `ebch_osd_awgn_campaign` runs one thread (observed: `Threads: 1`, 99.7% of one core on a 24-thread host during the 2026-08-27 rigorous campaign). The crate ships rayon and a parallel executor stack that the other campaign binaries (`dvb_t2_awgn_campaign`, `ldpc_bler_sweep`) already use; the OSD tool predates none of it. The dominant grid cell (order-2, 5.23 dB, ~4e7 blocks) pays the full cost.

Statistical correctness is unaffected; this is throughput only.

## Fix sketch

Converge on the crate's deterministic-parallelism convention (convention-convergence) instead of a bespoke mechanism: `gf2_sim::parallel` (design doc §3, §11) already provides the per-worker ChaCha20 word-position seek (`worker_offset`), per-worker contexts and counters (`WorkerCtx`), and fixed-order reduction, with byte-identical results across worker counts for a fixed seed. Blocks carry global indices independent of the executing worker, so the stopping rule becomes index-ordered truncation: a cell completes at the smallest block index whose in-order cumulative block-error count reaches K, and blocks evaluated speculatively past that index contribute to no counter. The evaluator contract moves off `FnMut` to per-worker evaluators; the campaign binary adapts.

Adopting worker-seeked streams changes the sampled block sequence relative to the retired serial binary; that is a new behavioral identity recorded in provenance as usual. The identity contract becomes worker-count invariance, with the single-worker run as the reference.

## Success Criteria

- REQ-01: The protocol evaluates blocks on multiple threads while committing outcomes in block-index order; for a fixed campaign and seed, all counters, the stopping index, and the receipt payload are byte-identical across worker counts (single-worker run as reference), demonstrated at least for {1, 2, 8, 24}.
- REQ-02: The stopping design is preserved structurally: completion exactly at the block carrying the K-th block error; speculative blocks beyond it contribute to no counter.
- REQ-03: A test compares multi-worker and single-worker runs of a scripted evaluator and asserts identical results; existing resume and protocol tests pass, with byte-identity fixtures re-pinned to the new behavioral identity where the stream change requires it.
- REQ-04: Worker count defaults to available parallelism, is settable via a CLI flag, and appears in the receipt's invocation argv provenance.
- REQ-05: Measured speedup on an order-2 probe cell on the 24-thread host is reported in the issue closure notes.
- REQ-06: Parallelism is driven through the existing `gf2_sim::parallel` primitives (worker-offset seek discipline, ordered reduction); any deviation is a named tracked exception cited in rustdoc and backed by a tracker issue (convention-convergence).
title: OSD campaign protocol evaluates blocks single-threaded, idling 23 of 24 host threads
